what_it_does: Generative AI requires hardware acceleration for two very different types of models with opposite computational patterns. Standard models like transformers do inference in one pass. Diffusion models (used for image generation) solve the problem iteratively, repeating the same network 25 to 100 times, making them vastly more compute-hungry. A single-architecture accelerator does both poorly. This paper presents MEGA.mini, a processor with a heterogeneous design: large processor cores optimized for single-pass transformers and convolutional networks, paired with smaller cores tuned for diffusion's repetitive workload. This approach adapts compute and power efficiency to whichever model type is running.
